transcript: Last night, I saw The Animal Kingdom in the upstairs theater of the Connelly in the East Village. This is being produced and directed by Jack Serio, who recently did the Uncle Vanya in Flatiron. This piece was similar in that David Cromer's in it, and it's similar in quality. (spoiler alert, it’s really good) In it, we see five characters: Four family members and a therapist in a series of group therapy sessions, In the aftermath of one of the family members having had… I’ll just say severe self-destructive behaviors but trigger warnings galore. It’s about 80 minutes of pure tension and the dynamics are fascinating to witness in such an intimate, almost claustrophobic space. You really feel like a fly on the wall. The entire cast is fantastic, but I wanted to highlight Calvin Leon Smith who was recently seen in Fat Ham. Here, he plays the therapist and gives such a delicate and seemingly effortless performance. The Animal Kingdom was just extended through next Saturday the 17th and I suspect tickets are hard to come by but keep an eye out if you're around. With that, another program for my collection.
